examples.question_text:
Use helpful factors to calculate mentally:
(a) $38\times5$
(b) $68\times25$.

Calculate mentally by regrouping helpful factors:
(a) $72\times125$
(b) $54\times50$.
Factorise both $26$ and $35$ to form a factor of $10$, then calculate $26\times35$.

For $42\times25$:
(a) find two helpful factorisations of $42$ and use one to calculate the product
(b) complete $42\times25=\square\times50$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $42=21\times2$ and $42=7\times6$.
The first pairs $2$ with $25$ to make $50$; the second pairs $6$ with $25$ to make $150$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}42\times25\\&=21\times2\times25\\&=21\times50\\&=1050\end{aligned}$
(b) Since $2\times25=50$, the remaining factor is $21$.
$\square=21$

examples.question_text:
(a) A student writes $22\times25=11\times2\times25=11\times100$. Identify the error and give the correct product.
(b) Explain why $(3\times8)\times7=3\times(8\times7)$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $22=11\times2$ is correct, but $2\times25=50$, not $100$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}22\times25\\&=11\times2\times25\\&=11\times50\\&=550\end{aligned}$
(b) Both sides use the same factors in the same order. Only the grouping changes.
Both sides equal $168$.

examples.derivation: 38×5=19×2×5=19×10=190; 68×25=17×4×25=17×100=1700. Both preserve the source's factorisation-and-regrouping strategy and the existing mathematics.
72×125=9×8×125=9×1000=9000; 54×50=27×2×50=27×100=2700. The useful existing applications remain mathematically unchanged and introduce no new method beyond retained assessment adaptations.
26=13×2 and 35=7×5, so 26×35=13×2×7×5=13×7×10=91×10=910. Factoring both numbers extends the supplied regrouping strategy consistently with the retained assessed method.
42=21×2=7×6; 2×25=50 and 6×25=150. Hence 42×25=21×50=1050, and the missing factor is 21. The supplementary scaffolding and all original mathematical content are preserved.

2×25=50, so 22×25=11×2×25=11×50=550; replacing 2×25 by 100 doubles the product incorrectly. (3×8)×7=24×7=168 and 3×(8×7)=3×56=168. Retaining this existing supplementary explanation is explicitly authorised; it does not reinstate either removed assessment.
